feed.head: σειρίασις
feed.why: The split form writes the accented ι, so it must keep its own accent (σειρίᾱσις, like ψωρίασις). The visible head σειρίασις is already right; only orth_orig 'σειρι-ᾱσις' lacks the accent. Repair orth_orig to σειρί-ᾱσις, as B prints.

feed.head: σειραῖος
feed.why: The conjecture replaces genitive σειρίου, and 'sc. ἵππου' needs a genitive adjective. The acute on -αί- is also correct only before long -ου (a short -ον would need σειραῖον). So the reading is σειραίου; current σειραίον is a ν/υ misreading.

feed.head: σεβαστικός
feed.why: The work cited is Iamblichus' VP (Vita Pythagorica), and the same article already cites Iamb. Protr. 21. Current 'lamb.' is an l/I misreading of the author abbreviation.

feed.head: σεβασμιότης
feed.why: σεβασμιότης is a common abstract noun ('Reverence, as a title'); LSJ capitalises only proper names, and B prints lower case. The capital follows the starred key, which is unreliable here: the nearby σεβαστικός has a starred key but a lower-case head. Repair head to σεβασμιότης and orth_orig to σεβασμ-ιότης.

feed.head: σάρξ
feed.why: The etymology compares Avest. θwarəs-, whose s is the Iranian outcome of a palatal k̂. B's circumflexed k̂ marks that palatal, which the comparison needs; current's plain twrk- drops a meaningful diacritic.

feed.head: σαργίον
feed.why: LSJ's 'sq.' means the following article, so the later bracket '[σαργίον]' resolves it to this article's own headword. That makes the gloss say σαργίον = σαργίον. The addition is unsupported and misleading; B's printed '= sq.' without it is the supported reading.

feed.head: σάλος
feed.why: In S. OT 24 the adjective qualifies genitive σάλου ('of the bloody swell'); current φοινίον (acc./neut.) cannot agree with σάλου and is a ν/υ misreading. B's φοινίου is the grammatical reading.

feed.head: σαικωνέω
feed.why: A variant after 'or', marked as a suffix form (extent=suff), must share the headword's stem σαικων-, and 'cf. σαλακωνίζω' points to a -κωνίζω formation. Current's σαθρ-ίζω has an unrelated stem, does not fit the meaning 'move', and breaks the alphabetical order. B's σαικων-ίζω is the coherent reading.

feed.head: σαγήνη
feed.why: Both witnesses have the letter C; only its case differs. A capital letter in parentheses after a lemma is LSJ's homonym marker, so ἐπίπλοος (C) points to the third homonym, which fits this sense. A lowercase (c) could be misread as a subsense label. B keeps the standard form.

feed.head: Σαββατίζω
feed.why: Current's own key and id (*sabba^ti/zw) keep the source capital, and B agrees with Σαββᾰτ-ίζω. Only the visible head and orth_orig were lowercased, which normalises away the printed capital. Repair: restore Σ in <head> (Σαββατίζω) and in orth_orig (Σαββᾰτ-ίζω).

feed.head: σ
feed.why: The article calls this form 'the old eighteenth letter' and says σάν was originally its name. That letter is san, Ϻ, not capital Mu, which is the thirteenth letter. B's Ϻ is correct; current's Μ misidentifies the letter.

feed.head: ῥυπάω
feed.why: Current's ἄφλιον is not a Greek word. It is a φ/θ slip (beta-code f for q). In the quoted string of adjectives (ῥυπῶντα, κυφόν, ...) for Ar. Pl. 266, only ἄθλιον fits. B has the real word.

feed.head: ῥήμων
feed.why: The old v.l. ῥήμονες comes from re-dividing καί ῥ’ ἥμονες in Il.23.886, so the ῥ’ is essential to the note. Current's raw XML shows a double space (καί  ἥμονες) where it dropped out.

feed.head: ῥήγνυμι
feed.why: LSJ equates the dialect participle ἐρρηγεῖα with the regular -υῖα. Current lost the '=' in Greek context, leaving a stray leading space inside the etym tag ' -υῖα', so the equation now reads as a bare variant. B preserves (= -υῖα).

feed.head: ῥέω
feed.why: Both witnesses mark the short vowels of the alternating roots srǒw- and srǔ- with a caron. B's srěw- follows that same convention, while current's grave è has no meaning in this Indo-European root notation.

feed.head: ῥεαντής
feed.why: λεαντής 'polisher' is a common noun postulated to explain ῥεαντής, so current's capital Λ is wrong. It comes from an asterisk being read as a capital marker. B keeps the printed *λεαντής, with the asterisk marking an unattested form.

feed.head: ῥαχία
feed.why: After 'Nonn.' the note refers back to the places already cited (Nonn.D.11.182, 39.334), i.e. the LSJ abbreviation ll.cc. (locis citatis). Current's capital 'Il.cc.' is a misreading that wrongly suggests the Iliad.

feed.head: ῥαίω
feed.why: Od. 9.459 reads τῷ κέ οἱ ἐγκέφαλός: dative enclitic οἱ is unaccented before non-enclitic ἐγκέφαλός (κέ takes the acute); current οἵ would be the relative plural and is wrong.

feed.head: Ϙ ϙ
feed.why: Everything the article cites is early: the Etruscan abecedaria, Locrian inscriptions of v B.C., and the numeral 90 in iii B.C. papyri. All use the Q-shaped archaic koppa Ϙ ϙ, not the later zigzag Ϟ ϟ. The visible head and orth_orig both read Ϟ ϟ, so both should be repaired to Ϙ ϙ.

feed.head: σάν
feed.why: Current has only a [see print copy] placeholder for the medieval-manuscript form of the 900 sign. B supplies the minuscule sampi ϡ, which is that form, while still marking unencodable variants elsewhere with notes. So ϡ reflects the printed glyph and fills the gap.

feed.head: σάν
feed.why: Current's Τ is Greek tau (value 300), the wrong letter for the T-shaped later form of the 900 sign on Athenian tesserae. B uses the same archaic-sampi character here and for the Ionic σσ letter, so the printed glyph is the same in both places. Current writes that glyph as capital Ͳ, so Ͳ keeps the article consistent; B's lowercase ͳ would not.

feed.head: σάν
feed.why: Current has lost the glyph ('the numerical symbol  (= 900) ... which has this form'), and the sentence needs a symbol. The sign for 900 is sampi, and B supplies Ϡ, keeping it distinct from the later forms it marks separately.

feed.head: σάν
feed.why: The glyph is an alternative way of writing the sound s alongside Σ (the Etruscan twenty-first letter), so it must be a sigma form. Current's ϟ is the koppa character, the subject of the next article, and cannot stand for s. B's 𐌔 encodes the three-stroke sigma.

feed.head: σάν
feed.why: Current drops the opening parenthesis (leaving 'Syria 6.103)' unbalanced) and the Hebrew צ, and puts the word Sadi where the Phoenician glyph stands. B keeps '(צ, Phoenician 𐤑' but adds its own note '[glyph variant of Phoenecian Sadi]', which is not LSJ text. The replacement begins with a space and yields: Tsade (צ, Phoenician 𐤑 Syria 6.103).
